# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 2303
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/2303
- **Title**: fix(2256): viewer tail re-anchors when the session file shrinks below the cursor
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/2256-viewer-tail-reanchor` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +357
- **Deletions**: -10
- **Created**: 2026-11-18T12:33:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-11-18T15:15:17Z

## PR Description

## Problem

`FileSessionEventSource` tails the primary session JSONL with a growth-only line cursor (`total > start`). Every legal rewrite of the primary — segment rotation (80 MB, seeds a fresh header-only primary), hard-cap truncation (95 MB, drops the oldest lines) and open-time quarantine heal (drops torn lines) — SHRINKS the file below `_deliveredLines`. A shrink matches no branch: the cursor stays stale, every new record stays invisible until the primary regrows past the old count, and the viewer freezes forever — "you are viewing" over a dead transcript with no recovery transition.

## Fix

One check at the tail-follow boundary (`file_attachment.dart`):

- **Identity cursor** — the watcher now also remembers the record id of the last delivered line (`_lastRecordIds`, per session; a torn tail line decodes to nothing and never regresses the anchor).
- **Shrink branch (`total < start`)** — re-anchors instead of freezing: backward scan for the anchor id in the rewritten file; resume right after it when it survived (hard-cap shape → no duplicated/skipped rows even when truncation and appends land in the same poll gap), replay from the head when it is gone (rotation shape → everything surviving is unseen). Forward-only; history still comes from the normal open path (no cross-part tailing, per the card's non-goal).
- **Recovery transition surfaced** — the shrink emits `AttachedSessionEvent(reanchored: true)` even when it carries no rows, so the transition is never silent. Consumers: the CLI viewer prints `session file rotated/truncated — re-anchored viewer` (`sessionReanchorNotice`); the app's `AttachedSessionController` exposes `reanchorNotice`.

## Tests (TDD, red-first)

Red was proven before the fix: all three new `attach_test.dart` scenarios failed on the frozen watcher (only the backlog event ever arrived). Green after:

- **AC1** rotation shape: 10-row session → primary rewritten to header-only (+ torn-line variant) → re-anchor event fires, post-rotation records stream (today: never).
- **AC2** hard-cap shape: 12-row session + 5 unseen records + truncate-to-tail rewrite in one poll gap → exactly the 5 unseen rows emitted, kept rows not duplicated, none skipped; tail keeps streaming after.
- **AC3** e2e in `agent_cli_viewer_test.dart`: a live CLI viewer prints the recovery notice when the primary is rewritten under it and streams post-rewrite rows; `attached_session_controller_test.dart` pins the notice state.
- **AC4 REG** existing backlog/growth/multi-session tests unchanged and passing; plus a sibling-watch test proving a shrink re-anchors only its own session (per-session cursor map).

## Gates

- `dart test test/session/attach/attach_test.dart` — 23/23.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_viewer_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_attach_test.dart` — 17/17.
- `flutter test test/attach/attached_session_controller_test.dart` (standalone Flutter 3.50.0, the CI pin) — 4/4.
- `dart analyze` (touched paths + full root: no issues in touched files; remaining root findings are pre-existing sub-package resolution noise), `flutter analyze` on changed app files — clean.
- `dart format` — exact (0 changed).

Fixes #2256

# Review Policy

Preset: `default` — resolved from: built-in default (resolution chain: projectConfig.reviewPolicy → workflow jobParams → built-in default).
Verification: `none` — findings post exactly as the review leg raised them — no second-stage verification.
Every verdict on this PR is traceable to this table.

| Severity | Round | Fix | Gates approval |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🚨 BLOCKING | rework | mandatory | YES |
| ⚠️ IMPORTANT | rework | mandatory | YES |
| 💡 SUGGESTION | polish | mandatory | no |
| 🪶 NIT | none | opportunistic | no |

Verification: `none` — findings post exactly as the review leg raised them — no second-stage verification.

Bounds: polishMaxThreads=6 · polishMaxChangedLines=80 · opportunisticMaxThreads=8 · opportunisticSameFilesOnly=true · densityMin=2 · densityMax=8 · sweepBatch=10 · sweepMaxAgeDays=30

Density cap (💡/🪶 threads only; 🚨/⚠️ never capped): allowed = clamp(round(2 + 3*sqrt(additions/200)), 2, 8).
Rank your findings and post the top-K as threads; the overflow becomes a ranked digest list in the general comment. The census counts posted threads + digest lines.

Machine enforcement: the approval is recomputed from the severity census + this policy — the model verdict is advisory. Any 🚨 or ⚠️ open → REQUEST_CHANGES; only 💡/🪶 → APPROVE.
## Downgrade protocol

A rework lap may downgrade a specific ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only with a written justification** in the census (the thread reply and the response summary: why this is not maintainability debt). A silent downgrade does not exist: the next review round re-raises it as ⚠️ IMPORTANT and the cycle repeats. A justified downgrade lets a false-⚠️ review converge to APPROVE without a code change.

# pr-2303: fix(2256): viewer tail re-anchors when the session file shrinks below the cursor

## Description

## Problem

`FileSessionEventSource` tails the primary session JSONL with a growth-only line cursor (`total > start`). Every legal rewrite of the primary — segment rotation (80 MB, seeds a fresh header-only primary), hard-cap truncation (95 MB, drops the oldest lines) and open-time quarantine heal (drops torn lines) — SHRINKS the file below `_deliveredLines`. A shrink matches no branch: the cursor stays stale, every new record stays invisible until the primary regrows past the old count, and the viewer freezes forever — "you are viewing" over a dead transcript with no recovery transition.

## Fix

One check at the tail-follow boundary (`file_attachment.dart`):

- **Identity cursor** — the watcher now also remembers the record id of the last delivered line (`_lastRecordIds`, per session; a torn tail line decodes to nothing and never regresses the anchor).
- **Shrink branch (`total < start`)** — re-anchors instead of freezing: backward scan for the anchor id in the rewritten file; resume right after it when it survived (hard-cap shape → no duplicated/skipped rows even when truncation and appends land in the same poll gap), replay from the head when it is gone (rotation shape → everything surviving is unseen). Forward-only; history still comes from the normal open path (no cross-part tailing, per the card's non-goal).
- **Recovery transition surfaced** — the shrink emits `AttachedSessionEvent(reanchored: true)` even when it carries no rows, so the transition is never silent. Consumers: the CLI viewer prints `session file rotated/truncated — re-anchored viewer` (`sessionReanchorNotice`); the app's `AttachedSessionController` exposes `reanchorNotice`.

## Tests (TDD, red-first)

Red was proven before the fix: all three new `attach_test.dart` scenarios failed on the frozen watcher (only the backlog event ever arrived). Green after:

- **AC1** rotation shape: 10-row session → primary rewritten to header-only (+ torn-line variant) → re-anchor event fires, post-rotation records stream (today: never).
- **AC2** hard-cap shape: 12-row session + 5 unseen records + truncate-to-tail rewrite in one poll gap → exactly the 5 unseen rows emitted, kept rows not duplicated, none skipped; tail keeps streaming after.
- **AC3** e2e in `agent_cli_viewer_test.dart`: a live CLI viewer prints the recovery notice when the primary is rewritten under it and streams post-rewrite rows; `attached_session_controller_test.dart` pins the notice state.
- **AC4 REG** existing backlog/growth/multi-session tests unchanged and passing; plus a sibling-watch test proving a shrink re-anchors only its own session (per-session cursor map).

## Gates

- `dart test test/session/attach/attach_test.dart` — 23/23.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_viewer_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_attach_test.dart` — 17/17.
- `flutter test test/attach/attached_session_controller_test.dart` (standalone Flutter 3.50.0, the CI pin) — 4/4.
- `dart analyze` (touched paths + full root: no issues in touched files; remaining root findings are pre-existing sub-package resolution noise), `flutter analyze` on changed app files — clean.
- `dart format` — exact (0 changed).

Fixes #2256

`dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart`: grouped **APPEND-ONLY** export
  sections — one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted by path
  within a group, new exports append to their group. No mini-barrels, no
  re-sorting (gh-1232).
- God-file ceiling: no `.dart` file over **2800** lines (crap4dart `loc`
  gate). Target < 2000 for primary files; split by concern into `part`
  files — never by extracting public API.

## Working in parallel (shared checkout + worktrees)

Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked; run no
heavy commands (full suites/analyze) in it; never `git stash` the user's
WIP; talk to peer agents through the messaging fabric, not their files.
Worktrees only if genuinely required — ask first, create detached under
`.worktrees/<name>/` from the remote tracking ref, remove when done.
Full policy: `docs/agents/parallel-worktrees.md`.

## Memory (footnote)

Before any non-trivial task, **search memory first** (`memory_search`,
then `memory_list` for fuzzy topics). Scopes: **project** = this repo
(`.fah/memory/note/` since gh-2185 — local-only, not committed; the
user's files: read freely, write only via `memory_add`), **user** = global/private. `memory_add` stores durable facts
only; supersede by delete + add — never leave solved problems to rot. The
host recomposes the `<memory>` prompt section after every add; tool wiring
is `memoryTools` + `lib/src/memory/`. Churn pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`;
usage details: `docs/agents/memory-usage.md`.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done: coverage first (`test/goldens/` + `golden_guard_test.dart`
map), real fonts (`ensureGoldenFonts`), full frames (1280x800 / 390x844),
determinism, eyes on pixels after `--update-goldens`, green
`flutter test test/goldens` + `scripts/check_goldens.py` (orphan snapshots
hard-fail). Full rules: `docs/agents/golden-tests.md`.

## Prompts live outside Dart code

Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (YAML frontmatter,
`{{token}}` placeholders) — never string literals in `.dart`. After
editing: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` regenerates the `.g.dart`
files (`test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` gates drift); Codex catalog
refresh: `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Details:
`docs/agents/prompts.md`.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The hook is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI classifies
PRs through the same script (`--dry-run`) — one classifier, one threshold
set, hook/CI parity via `GATE_STAGE` markers. Path rules: docs/markdown/
prompts-only → size + analyze; lib/bin/test/pubspec → +tests, coverage,
CRAP, dup, dupx; `test/integration/**` → +integration-mock;
flutter_app/packages → +flutter; scripts/.github → everything. Invariants:

- analyze + format clean; `dart test` green — **deterministic-only**
  (mock LLM; live models never in the gate; `llm`-tagged files run only in
  the tag-only provider smoke + nightly).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80%; jscpd < 1% core / < 3.7% app; cross-module
  dup < 0.31%; CRAP ratchet: core 12.0, app 30.0 (thresholds only-down);
  ≤ 2800 lines per `.dart` file; AGENTS.md ceiling (top of this file).
- Red-in-≥2-distinct-SHA-runs flakes quarantine via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json`; nightly keeps running quarantined files.

Full gate text: `docs/agents/quality-gates.md`; CI workflows: `docs/ci.md`.

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type exists on BOTH the CLI
and the Flutter app unless fundamentally impossible — then it MUST be in
`cliOnlySettings`/`appOnlySettings` (`lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`)
with the reason; run `dart test test/parity/`. Host capabilities (issue
#1079): every host-wiring capability declares its 7-host matrix state AT
BIRTH (`on` / `off(reason)` / `transport`) via `wireAgentCore` — `off` is
invisible everywhere; extensions are declared surface, SDK invariants have
no override point. Full rules: `docs/agents/cross-platform-parity.md`.

## Commits and releases

- Commit as `ai.teammate <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (set repo-locally);
  subjects `type(scope): ...`. Release-path automation MUST use the
  fa-release-bot GitHub App token — never a PAT or `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Every push to main cuts an annotated tag (`scripts/auto_release.sh`);
  the tag is the single version source (pubspecs stay `0.0.0-dev`);
  releases go DRAFT-first and publish at `release-provenance` only with
  signed SHA256SUMS attached. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only (`## Unreleased`).
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag (first publish of a new
  package is manual); every lockfile is committed and enforced
  (`scripts/check_lockfiles.sh`); TestFlight external-group + store

`IoExecutionEnv` (the production local host) and `MemoryExecutionEnv` both implement `RenamableFileSystem`. `execution_env.dart:242` says hosts that don't advertise it "degrade to unenforced" — so on non-rename hosts rotation is unenforced/absent... `session_repo.dart:700` — `if (_fs is! RenamableFileSystem)` → presumably rotation suspended at open → the truncation-only cap path becomes the mainline on such hosts. Which hosts are non-rename? Possibly the web/hosted ones. So on a non-rename host, hard-cap truncation is the ONLY cap mechanism, and every cap-append is drop-k+append-1 → count-neutral skips are routine there whenever a viewer is attached. That firms up finding A: on rename-capable hosts (CLI/macOS mainline) it needs suspended rotation or monster records; on non-rename hosts the truncation-only cap IS the steady state. Still ⚠️ IMPORTANT (not 🚨 — no data loss in the session file itself; the viewer misses rows; mainline hosts have rename), but with a sharper reachability statement.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The re-anchor fix works for the rotation and net-shrink hard-cap shapes (all gates verified: attach 23/23, CLI 17/17, controller 4/4, analyze/format clean), but the count-based shrink trigger and the last-line anchor leave three proven holes in the same boundary this PR rewrites: a count-neutral rewrite silently skips records forever, one unreadable poll resets the cursor and replays the whole transcript as duplicates, and a never-set anchor re-emits surviving rows after a quarantine heal. Each hole was verified with an executable repro against this branch's `FileSessionEventSource`.

**Key Issues** (⚠️ IMPORTANT — inline threads):
1. `file_attachment.dart:73` — the shrink branch keys on `total < start` only; a count-neutral rewrite (hard-cap drop-1 + append-1 in one poll gap) matches no branch and the appended record is silently skipped forever.
2. `file_attachment.dart:81` — `lines == null` (unreadable/missing, e.g. the rotation rename→seed window) is conflated with an empty file: the shrink branch fires on a file that did not shrink, resets the cursor to 0, and the next poll replays the entire transcript as a non-reanchored growth event.
3. `file_attachment.dart:107` — the anchor is never set when the last line is torn at every poll (viewer attached to a crashed session); the quarantine heal then shrinks with a null anchor and re-emits every surviving record.

**Digest**:
- `flutter_app/lib/services/attached_session_controller.dart:45` — `reanchorNotice` is exposed but no widget renders it; the app user never sees the recovery transition (ticket AC satisfied literally — the CLI renders it).
- `lib/src/session/attach/file_attachment.dart:125` — doc reference `[._recordIdOf]` is malformed; `[_recordIdOf]` is the convention.

**Next Steps**:
1. Extend the rewrite trigger past count: also treat `total == start` with a changed last-record id as a rewrite (same resume path), and skip the poll entirely when `lines == null` (unreadable ≠ empty).
2. Derive the anchor from the last parseable line (backward scan past torn lines) instead of strictly `lines.last`.
3. Cover the three shapes with attach_test scenarios (count-neutral cap append, unreadable poll, baseline-torn-tail heal).

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: count-neutral rewrite silently skips records forever**

The shrink branch keys on `total < start` only. A rewrite that lands with an **unchanged line count** matches no branch (`total == start`), so the newly appended record is never delivered and no re-anchor event fires — the viewer silently stops streaming, which is exactly the failure family this PR claims to close ("no duplicated/skipped rows even when truncation and appends land in the same poll gap").

Proven against this branch (`FileSessionEventSource`, pollInterval 0): deliver 12 rows → in one poll gap drop the oldest record **and** append a new one (count-neutral hard-cap shape) → no event fires at all; the next append delivers only the newer record, proving the middle one is skipped forever.

Production reachability: `_truncateOldestLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:1834`) drops the minimum k oldest records and the caller appends 1 record in the same locked envelope — count-neutral whenever k == 1 (uniform record sizes at the 95 MB cap). That path is the steady state when rotation is suspended (failed part listing at open) or when `_rotateSegmentLocked` fails and falls through to the cap on the un-rotated segment; a quarantine heal (drop j torn lines) plus j appends in one gap lands the same way. (Note: the same `total == start` mechanism also hides a torn line that completes between polls — pre-existing, but this change is the moment to close the whole class.)

Suggested fix: detect the rewrite by identity, not count — when `total == start` and `_lastIdOf(lines) != _lastRecordIds[sessionId]`, run the same resume path as the shrink branch. Then add an attach_test scenario for the drop-1 + append-1 gap (AC2's test only covers the net-shrink shape).

The next successful poll then takes the growth branch from 0 and re-emits **every already-delivered row as a `reanchored: false` growth event** — the viewer appends the entire transcript a second time.

Proven against this branch (pollInterval 0): deliver 5 rows → one poll where `resolvePath` returns null (or the read fails) → event 2 is the empty re-anchor marker → event 3 replays `m0..m4` with `reanchored: false` → duplicated rows.

Production reachability: the CLI viewer resolves a fixed path (`agent_cli_viewer.dart:253`), so the trigger is `readTextLines` failing — concretely the rotation window in `_rotateSegmentLocked` (`renamePath(primary → part)` then `writeFile(seed)`: a viewer read landing between the two gets ENOENT; the storage lock guards writers, not the viewer's reads). There the follow-up replay is benign (the reseeded primary is header-only), but a transient read failure with the file unchanged produces the full duplicate replay. The app wiring (`cli_session_presence.dart:100`) takes a caller-supplied nullable `resolvePath`, so a session momentarily missing from a listing triggers it there too. Note the pre-PR code was immune by accident: `0 < start` matched no branch, so an unreadable poll was simply ignored.

Suggested fix: skip the round when the read failed — after the baseline, `lines == null` should leave cursor and anchor untouched (unreadable ≠ empty); only `lines != null && total < start` is a genuine shrink.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: anchor never set when the tail is torn — quarantine heal replays every surviving record as duplicates**

`_anchorId` only stores the id when the **last** line decodes. If the watcher's baseline (or every poll since it) observes a torn tail line, `_lastRecordIds[sessionId]` stays absent — and a later shrink takes the `anchorId == null → return 0` path here, treating the **whole surviving file as unseen** and re-emitting records the viewer already delivered.

Proven against this branch (pollInterval 0): seed 2 records, append a torn tail line **before** the watcher's first poll (viewer attached to a crashed session) → backlog delivers `m0, m1`, torn line counted in the cursor, anchor never set → quarantine heal rewrites the primary from the surviving records (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:1431` — the open path drops torn lines) → the re-anchor event carries `m0, m1` **again** → duplicated rows in the viewer.

This is one of the three shrink shapes the PR description names as handled ("open-time quarantine heal (drops torn lines)"); the torn-line design note ("decodes to nothing and never regresses the anchor") covers the *regression* case but misses the *never set* case. The realistic sequence is: session crashes mid-write → user opens the viewer to inspect it → user restarts the CLI → the open heals the primary while the watch is live.

Suggested fix: derive the anchor from the last **parseable** line instead of strictly `lines.last` — a backward scan over `lines` for the last decodable record id (mirroring `_resumeIndex`'s backward scan) makes the anchor land on the last actually-delivered record even when the tail is torn.

All verification passed. The review is complete — the tree is back to the exact PR state (0 modified files) and the touched test suite is green on that final state.

## Review summary — PR #2303 (fix/2256-viewer-tail-reanchor)

**Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES** — 3 ⚠️ IMPORTANT findings, all verified with executable repros I ran against this branch's `FileSessionEventSource` (scratch test, since deleted).

The re-anchor fix itself is well-built for its headline shapes: rotation and net-shrink hard-cap truncation re-anchor correctly, all four ticket ACs have passing tests, and every claimed gate reproduced green (attach 23/23, CLI 17/17, controller 4/4 with CI's `.env` placeholder, analyze + format clean). But the count-based trigger and last-line anchor leave three proven holes in the exact boundary this PR rewrites:

1. **`file_attachment.dart:73`** — a count-neutral rewrite (hard-cap drop-1 + append-1 in one poll gap) matches `total == start`: no branch fires, the appended record is silently skipped forever. Proven: no event on the rewrite; the next append delivers only the newer row.
2. **`file_attachment.dart:81`** — `lines == null` (unreadable/missing — e.g. the rotation rename→seed window a viewer read can land in) is conflated with an empty file: the shrink branch fires on a file that didn't shrink, resets the cursor to 0, and the next poll replays the entire transcript as a non-reanchored growth event. Proven: 5 delivered rows → one unreadable poll → all 5 re-emitted as duplicates.
3. **`file_attachment.dart:107`** — the anchor is never set when the tail is torn at every poll (viewer attached to a crashed session); the quarantine heal then shrinks with a null anchor → `_resumeIndex` returns 0 → every surviving record is re-emitted. Proven: 2 delivered rows → heal → `m0, m1` delivered again.

Digest (non-thread): `reanchorNotice` is exposed on the app controller but no widget renders it; malformed doc reference `[._recordIdOf]` at `file_attachment.dart:125`.
